sanskrit_verse:
ग्रामसीमासु च बहिर् ये स्युस् तत्कृषिजीविनः।
गोपशाकुनिकव्याधास् ते चान्ये वनगोचराः॥
transliteration: grāmasīmāsu ca bahir ye syus tatkṛṣijīvinaḥ | gopaśākunikavyādhās te cānye vanagocarāḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Those who dwell beyond village boundaries and live by tilling the land, as well as herders, fowl-keepers, hunters, and others who wander in forests—these beings are to be recognized as dwelling in accordance with their svadharma and natural capacity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from alignment with svadharma, not territorial dominance
Causation is traced through conscious choice and environmental harmony
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by natural role, not social rank
Restoration logic operates through recognition of svabhāva
Consciousness alignment occurs when dharma-svabhāva is honored
executable_legal_axioms: IF entity resides beyond settlement boundary AND engages in agrarian or forest-based livelihood THEN recognize svadharma-based jurisdiction
IF individual's conduct aligns with natural role THEN no punitive liability arises
IF action originates from svabhāva THEN restoration occurs through dharmic reaffirmation
IF person dwells in ecological harmony THEN legal integration follows natural order recognition
IF occupation reflects innate capacity THEN societal obligation is acknowledgment, not regulation
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, jurisdictional claims over individuals whose livelihoods align with natural roles must prioritize svadharma recognition over territorial codification. The threshold of responsibility lies in disruption of ecological-social balance, not in mere existence or activity within or beyond settlements.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that actions arising from svabhāva do not incur karmic misalignment unless harm disrupts cosmic order. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that such beings naturally sustain dharma through their presence. Responsibility is proportional to disruption, not identity. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that alignment with svadharma nullifies punitive causality.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Conduct svadharma affirmation ritual to realign displaced individuals
Establish dharmic council comprising elders and natural-role representatives
Facilitate community acknowledgment of ecological contribution
Reintegrate through yajña honoring natural roles
Implement śuddhi process to restore consciousness integrity
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This ruling restores natural jurisdiction, affirms svadharma as legal basis, upholds consciousness as the sole adjudicator, and establishes non-punitive reality as the foundation of Sanātana Nyāya.
